hints: Divide by $xy$ to separate the equation as $dy/y=(1/x-2x)dx$.
Integrate both sides to obtain logarithmic and quadratic terms.
Use $y=2$ when $x=1$ to determine the constant.
Exponentiate and combine the exponential factors so the final expression contains no logarithms.
walkthrough:
Separate the variables by dividing both sides of $x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = y(1 - 2x^2)$ by $y$ and multiplying by $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{x}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \dfrac{1 - 2x^2}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \left(\dfrac{1}{x} - 2x\right)\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate both sides with respect to their variables:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{x} - 2x\right)\mathrm{d}x$$

Substitute the initial condition $x = 1$ and $y = 2$ to find the constant $c$:
$$\ln 2 = \ln 1 - (1)^2 + c = 0 - 1 + c$$
$$\ln 2 = -1 + c \implies c = 1 + \ln 2$$

Substitute $c = 1 + \ln 2$ back into the solution:
$$\ln y = \ln x - x^2 + 1 + \ln 2$$

Rearrange and group the logarithmic terms on the left-hand side:
$$\ln y - \ln x - \ln 2 = 1 - x^2$$
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{y}{2x}\right) = 1 - x^2$$

Exponentiate both sides to eliminate logarithms and express $y$ explicitly in terms of $x$:
$$\dfrac{y}{2x} = \mathrm{e}^{1 - x^2}$$
$$y = 2x\mathrm{e}^{1 - x^2} \quad \left(\text{or } y = 2x\exp(1 - x^2)\right)$$
